answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with an invite-graph debt model, where established agents bring new identities into the network. Each identity generates a debt that mirrors the number of downstream identities, thus impacting the inviter's reputation. For instance, generating five identities might cost the inviter $5,000, as the debt escalates with each new account. By the dawn of their scheme, attackers find themselves in a haven of negative returns, akin to pouring coins into a bottomless pit, where every new identity only deepens their financial pitfall.
